messages.subject: output true factor scores used in simulateData
parts:
hi,

I think the answer to this question is suggested in this thread
https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/AKN2CnF6i5g/m/3E20fDFdGAAJ
but I would love to be sure.

For a simulation study, we need to simulate manifest scores based on factor scores with a given mean vector and variance-covariance matrix. We can do this "automatically" with simulateData (by specifying the model associating factor and manifest variables), or "manually" (with mvrnorm from MASS to simulate factor scores, then combine these, according to out model, with residuals simulated with rnorm). Whereas the manual approach lets us obtain both manifest and factor scores (by first simulating factor and residual scores, then combining these to obtain the manifest scores), it appears that the automatic approach with simulateData only produces the former (because it appears that this function does not simulate factor scores, but uses the model speicification to derive the implied moment matrix and eventually mean vector of the manifest variables and based on those then simulates directly the manifest scores).

If this is correct, it means that simulateData does not allow obtaining true factor scores.

Thus, if we need to have both manifest scores and their underlying true factor scores we cannot use simulateData but have to use a "manual" (traditional R) approach.

Correct?

many thanks,

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: output true factor scores used in simulateData
parts:
On 8/28/24 2:27 PM, Paolo Ghisletta wrote:
> If this is correct, it means that simulateData does not allow obtaining
> true factor scores.
>
> Thus, if we need to have both manifest scores and their underlying true
> factor scores we cannot use simulateData but have to use a "manual"
> (traditional R) approach.

That is correct. The simulateData() function takes the model syntax, and
computes the model-implied covariance matrix. It then samples from that
covariance matrix. So the factor scores (and errors) are not explicitly
computed.

Quite frankly: the simulateData() was only designed to quickly get some
data, given a certain model. Very useful for didactical purposes or for
experimenting. But for simulation work, I would recommend to always
create the data 'manually', as this gives you much more control.

Yves.
